prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: Earth-observation mission providing land, coastal and cryosphere imaging products with predictable latency and documented quality. The ground segment plans spacecraft activities, acquires data, keeps operations safe, generates and preserves products and records, and gives controlled service access. Outside the boundary: spacecraft, launch segment, external user processing environments.

Ground elements:
- Mission Control Center (alias Bluebell, local voice only): real-time ops authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, release of validated commands. Maintains the operational contact schedule, which controls console staffing, command readiness and telemetry coverage.
- Flight Dynamics Facility: orbit analysis, maneuver planning, access prediction, navigation products.
- Payload Processing Facility: payload processing, calibration control, product assessment, distribution staging.
- Network Control System: comms monitoring, operational traffic routing, connectivity status.
- Long Term Archive: authoritative repository for preserved mission data, products, processing records, operational evidence.
- User Services Portal: controlled external interface for product search, ordering, status, user support.
- Mission Planning System: imaging demand plus constraints to executable plans.
- Command Validation Gateway: rule-check barrier before commands are released for uplink.
- Telemetry Ingest Service: receives contact telemetry and feeds ops, engineering and processing.
- Orbit Determination Engine: tracking inputs to controlled orbit knowledge.
- Product Quality Service: product checks before dissemination.
- Primary Processing Cluster (nominal) and Backup Processing Cluster (failover).
- Ground Network Manager: antenna availability; confirms contacts fit station readiness and maintenance.

Antennas (shared resource under configuration control):
- North S-Band Antenna: nominal early-pass uplink and low-rate telemetry.
- South S-Band Antenna: alternate S-band, compatible for short-notice reassignment.
- Kiruna X-Band Antenna: high-rate payload downlink in European visibility.
- Svalbard X-Band Antenna: northern contacts, longer visibility.

Actors:
- Spacecraft Operations Team: safety, contacts, command authorization, nominal and contingency decisions.
- Flight Dynamics Team: orbit maintenance and navigation.
- Payload Calibration Team: payload performance, calibration parameters, quality trends.
- Cybersecurity Desk: security monitoring and escalation.

Requirements: continuous monitoring of safety-critical functions; every planned pass supported; business-hours engineering plus on-call. Routine functions autonomous; humans must authorize commanding and major configuration changes. Assurance relies on procedures, configuration management, segregation of duties, evidence retention, rehearsed contingencies and periodic redundancy verification.

New part:
S033: The Network Control System distributes station allocations, confirms antenna readiness states, and records the actual start and end times of each contact.
S034: Contact booking requests are submitted through the Mission Planning System with the required service type, antenna preference, minimum elevation, data volume expectation, and priority class.
S035: Routine contacts are frozen at the daily planning cut-off, while contingency contacts may be inserted later when approved operational justification is recorded.
S036: Conflicts are resolved first by spacecraft safety need, then by data timeliness need, then by efficient use of common ground resources.
S037: The Ground Network Manager is also known as Juniper in standing operational rosters.
S038: The Ground Network Manager arbitrates unresolved contact conflicts and verifies that station commitments remain consistent with maintenance windows and staffing limits.
S039: The Flight Dynamics Facility is also known as Mistral in legacy shift logs.
S040: Flight Dynamics Facility provides visibility predictions and antenna pointing support products to the planning process before contacts are released for execution.
S041: Orbit Determination Engine produces the Doppler Residual Report after each qualified tracking pass to support navigation trend assessment.
S042: Local station teams are responsible for antenna pre-pass configuration, frequency standard verification, time correlation checks, safety interlocks, and logging of any local anomalies.
S043: Station operators notify the Mission Control Center when local constraints could affect an approved contact, including equipment warm-up limits, access restrictions, or unexpected maintenance activity.
S044: Ground Network Manager issues the Antenna Deicing Notice when forecast icing or measured buildup threatens tracking performance.
S045: Weather constraints are assessed using local forecasts and real-time measurements for wind, precipitation, temperature, lightning risk, and atmospheric attenuation.
S046: X-band contacts may be downgraded or moved when heavy precipitation is expected to reduce the link margin below the approved operating threshold.
S047: S-band contacts are normally more tolerant of weather, but high winds or unsafe outdoor conditions can still make an antenna unavailable for service.
S048: The Telemetry Ingest Service receives contact status and data-flow indicators so that downstream processing can distinguish planned gaps from station-side interruptions.
S049: The Payload Processing Facility coordinates with Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster when a downlink allocation change alters expected processing load or delivery timing.
S050: Ground network management practices emphasize advance coordination, disciplined change approval, continuous monitoring during contacts, and post-contact reconciliation against the approved schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
